newsitem.title: USA: Bond holders to tune in to US West conference call.
newsitem.headline: Bond holders to tune in to US West conference call.

text.p: Bond holders will be listening closely to a conference call Thursday morning by U S West Media Group for indications of the company's desire to restructure its partnership with Time Warner Inc, market sources said.

According to published reports, U S West and Time Warner have reached a conceptual understanding that could involve US West assuming a portion of Time Warner's debt in exchange for additional cable assets.

Stuart Rossmiller, media and cable analyst for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, believes US West is unlikely to add significant debt to its balance sheet, noting the company would risk damaging its reputation with investors.
US West executives recently promised investors they were committed to retaining a solid investment-grade debt rating.

Rossmiller pointed out that a company spokesman was recently quoted saying, "there is no burning need to restructure." He believes spreads on Time Warner, rather than US West bonds, may be more at risk of temporarily widening depending on the outcome of Thursday's call.

"Time Warner bonds may widen by up to five basis points if US West shows a lack of interest in a restructuring. Investors who believe that the companies are half way to reaching a deal may be disappointed," he said.

Rossmiller would view any spread-widening of Time Warner debt as a buying opportunity as he believes Time Warner remains committed to finding a way to reduce its investment in cable assets and reduce debt with or without U.S. West's cooperation.

US West Media Group, the cable subsidiary of US West Inc, will hold a meeting with Wall Street analysts at 1000EST/1500GMT on Thursday. The company expects to release its year-end and fourth quarter earnings at around 800EST/1300GMT on Thursday, according to a US West spokesman.
